newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Patten extends friendship to HK's future leader.
newsitem.headline: Patten extends friendship to HK's future leader.

text.p: Hong Kong's Governor Chris Patten on Sunday said he and his government would extend a warm hand of friendship to the territory's first post-handover leader who will be selected this week.
But Patten also warned that he would not be able to agree on all issues with his successor, the chief executive designate.
"Once a chief executive designate is chosen, we will extend a warm hand of friendship," Patten said in his regular 'Letter to Hong Kong' broadcast over government-funded radio.
Next July 1, Patten will bow out of the British colony to make way for the first chief executive heading the territory as a Special Administrative Region under Chinese rule.
The chief executive will be chosen this Wednesday by the Selection Committee, a panel of 400 people handpicked by China.
But Patten added: "I don't wish to appear unrealistic. The chief executive and I are not going to be able to agree on everything."
